Pop open the tube and start chucking dice with family and friends! In Chicken!, players will be rolling dice each turn—pressing their luck to score more Chickens while avoiding those foxes. On a turn, a player must choose to roll all the dice passed to them or "Chicken Out" to roll fewer dice. Players will score points from the Chickens they roll, but they will bust (and score no points) if 3 or more foxes appear across their dice. For each Egg symbol rolled, a die is hatched from the Coop and then the active player will choose to reroll all of their blanks, eggs, and newly hatched dice, or they may score their points and pass the dice to the next player. If a player chooses to "Chicken Out" at the start of their turn, they lose a point for being a chicken, but they get to place all Yellow and Orange dice back into the Coop. The first player to reach 25 Points from their Chickens wins the game! Number of players: 2 - 8 Game duration: 6 mn Complexity: 1 / 5 Play Chicken! and 1414 other games online. Overview Welcome to Fox Hollow ! It is a lovely place, but it has a fox problem. As a farmer, your job is to raise Chickens while avoiding the Foxes. On your turn, roll dice to collect Chickens and hatch additional dice. You may push your luck for more points, but if you roll 3 or more Foxes , you bust and score nothing for the turn. The first player to reach 25 points wins the game. Components 1 Cloth Board 8 Player Tokens 4 White Dice (2 chickens, 2 eggs, 1 fox, 1 blank) 4 Yellow Dice (3 chickens, 1 egg, 1 fox, 1 blank) 4 Orange Dice (1 chicken, 1 double chicken, 2 foxes, 1 blank) Setup Place the Cloth Board within reach of all players. Each player chooses a Player Token and places it on the starting space. Set aside any unused Player Tokens. Arrange the Yellow Dice and Orange Dice in rows inside the Coop. The player who most recently held a chicken goes first. If no player has held a chicken, choose the starting player randomly. Give all 4 White Dice to the starting player. Playing Your Turn At the beginning of your turn, choose one of the following: Go For It! Chicken Out! Go For It! Take all the dice passed to you and roll them. Chicken Out! Return all Yellow and Orange Dice passed to you to the Coop. Lose 1 point. Take the 4 White Dice and roll them. Important: If you Chicken Out while your Player Token is still on the starting space, you do not lose 1 point. Resolving a Roll After rolling: Place all Chickens you rolled to the right. Place all Foxes you rolled to the left. Leave all Eggs and Blank Dice in the middle. Chickens can score points at the end of your turn. Foxes can cause you to bust. If you ever have 3 or more Foxes showing across all your dice, you immediately bust. Hatching Dice If you did not bust, hatch additional dice for each Egg you rolled. For each Egg: Take 1 die from the Coop. Add it to the dice in the middle. When adding dice: Add Yellow Dice first. Add Orange Dice only when no Yellow Dice remain in the Coop. Orange Dice are riskier, but they can also provide greater rewards. If no dice remain in the Coop: Do not add a die for that Egg. Newly added dice are treated as Blank Dice until they are rolled. Reroll or Stop After hatching dice, choose one of the following: Reroll Count Your Chickens Reroll You must reroll all dice remaining in the middle . This includes: Blank Dice Dice showing Eggs Newly hatched dice You receive only 1 reroll per turn .

[Rating: 1/10] Really boring dice rolling. It’s almost like Pickomino except the math doesn’t work out right, so there’s no game involved.

[Rating: 2/10] I've played a dozen games or so now, 2-player and 3-player, and do not understand where the fun is. No one I've played it with has enjoyed it.  No one ever chickened out as the odds seemed in your favour to not roll 3 foxes. So in every game I played, the winner was the first person to roll all yellow and orange dice without getting foxes.   I re-checked the rules a bunch of times in case I was playing it wrong, but couldn't find any evidence of that.  I'm extremely disappointed because the designer is great, the company is great, and the production is amazing and super inviting.

[Rating: 2/10] Pointless game on rails where even non gamers realize there is no reason not to push your luck. Many other simple push your luck dice games do the mechanism much better.

[Rating: 3/10] This is an easy to learn and smooth dice rolling game. But unfortunately to be honest, I don't get the point. I like how the dice pool you have to roll changes. But to "chicken out" and loose a point seems nonsense as the other option is to roll and loose either nothing or get points. So where is the risk? I would understand it if with more dice you will get more points as a basis and you have to decide if you try to get even more points or keep just the basis points. [Rating: 3/10] Starting player has an advantage and there is nothing to mitigate it.  There is little agency in the game, often there is one very obvious choice to make: Roll all the dice. Might be better to let players choose any new dice freely when hatching, rather than force a certain order or randomly drawing from a bag.  Box is too small to fit everything from the KS, super annoying.  High quality components!

[Rating: 3/10] Had high hopes for this one, as the production is great, but it really fell flat for me and all my friends.  The game feels under-developed. There is no decision making, just roll all the dice. For a push your luck game, there are no tense / exciting moments that are fundamental to the genre. It feels more like a simple roll-and-move race game masquerading as a push-you-luck game. With nothing to account for player order.   And sad that the kickstarter components don't even fit into the box :(

[Rating: 3/10] Not enough pushing in this push your luck game. The one reroll made everything substantial that happened seem to just be insanely bad luck and nothing else mattered much. The art style is also... something lol.

[Rating: 3/10] One decision before you roll. A half decision mid turn. Turn order binding that makes the game fairly static. And the game ends by a race condition that makes little sense with the length of the game. Even with the sparse decisions on offer, the game doesn't seem to understand risk at all, given the penalty to calling chicken or just continuing to roll in view of the fixed turn order and the hard stop race condition. Truly, this is just bad.
